certified and unexpired.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"For a US citizen, which document proves lawful status?","fact_ids":["sec10-F08"]},"answer":{"text":"The same document used to prove identity.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08"]},"rationale":{"text":"For a US citizen, the document used to prove identity also proves lawful status.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-F01"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Bringing the right documents","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Four categories.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]},{"text":"Identity documents.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]},{"text":"Lawful status documents.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on proving identity and lawful status. In this lesson you will learn the four kinds of proof a first-time applicant must bring, what renewing holders need for a Real ID-compliant card, which identity documents are accepted and under what conditions, what to show if your name or birth date has changed, and which documents prove lawful status in the United States. Keep this in mind as you practice. Read each practice question carefully. Match the question to the exact rule. Take it one rule at a time.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What to bring","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Identity, lawful status, Social Security number.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02"]},{"text":"Two Indiana residency documents.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02"]},{"text":"Renewing: originals for Real ID.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"A first-time applicant for a license, learner's permit or ID card must bring originals or verifiable certified copies proving identity, lawful status in the US and full Social Security number, plus two documents proving Indiana residency. Someone renewing, amending or replacing a current Indiana credential should bring original or certified documents to a branch if they want a Real ID-compliant credential. So a first-time applicant needs four kinds of proof, and a renewing holder needs documents mainly when moving to a Real ID-compliant card.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Birth certificates and passports","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Certified government birth certificate.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-F05"]},{"text":"No hospital souvenir certificates.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-F05"]},{"text":"Passports must be unexpired.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"A US birth certificate used as identity proof must be an original or certified copy issued by a government agency, and unofficial hospital birth certificates are not accepted. A US passport or passport card can prove identity only if it is not expired. A foreign passport proves identity only when it is unexpired and carries a US visa with an approved I-ninety-four form showing the most recent admission or current status. So each of these documents has a condition: certified for birth certificates, and unexpired for passports.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Other identity rules","fact_ids":["sec10-R04","sec10-F06","sec10-R05","sec10-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"DHS cards: unexpired and verified.","fact_ids":["sec10-R04","sec10-F06","sec10-R05","sec10-R06"]},{"text":"Delayed birth certificates: identity only.","fact_ids":["sec10-R04","sec10-F06","sec10-R05","sec10-R06"]},{"text":"Amended certificates: certified and filed.","fact_ids":["sec10-R04","sec10-F06","sec10-R05","sec10-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"A Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Card can prove identity only if it is unexpired and its lawful status has been verified. A person born outside the US may use a delayed birth certificate to prove identity, but not lawful status. An amended birth certificate showing a new legal name or date of birth must be certified and filed with the vital statistics office in the state of birth. A non-citizen who received a Real ID-compliant credential using one of the listed documents may use that credential as identity proof in later transactions.","fact_ids":["sec10-R04","sec10-F06","sec10-R05","sec10-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Name changes and lawful status","fact_ids":["sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R07","sec10-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Prove any name or birth date change.","fact_ids":["sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R07","sec10-R08"]},{"text":"Citizens: identity proves status.","fact_ids":["sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R07","sec10-R08"]},{"text":"Notice of Action; asylum proof.","fact_ids":["sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R07","sec10-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"If your legal name or date of birth differs from your identity documents, you must show legal proof of the change, such as a marriage license, divorce decree or court order. For a US citizen, the document used to prove identity also proves lawful status. A Notice of Action on Form I-seven-ninety-seven counts as lawful status proof when the BMV confirms DHS has received it and not denied the action. Proof of an asylum application verified by DHS is listed as a lawful status document. So lawful status is proven differently for citizens and non-citizens.","fact_ids":["sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R07","sec10-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The delayed certificate trap","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-F06","sec10-R01","sec10-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: one document proves everything.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-F06","sec10-R01","sec10-F03"]},{"text":"Delayed certificate: identity only.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-F06","sec10-R01","sec10-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. For a US citizen, one document does double duty, because the document used to prove identity also proves lawful status. It is tempting to assume every identity document works that way. A person born outside the US may use a delayed birth certificate to prove identity, but not lawful status, which must be shown another way. A second trap involves hospital certificates. Unofficial hospital birth certificates are not accepted; the birth certificate must be an original or certified copy issued by a government agency.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-F06","sec10-R01","sec10-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a citizen's status","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-F01","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"US citizen.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-F01","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},{"text":"Which document proves lawful status?","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-F01","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: for a US citizen, which document proves lawful status? Recall the rule. For a US citizen, the document used to prove identity also proves lawful status. So the answer is the same document used to prove identity, such as a certified government birth certificate or an unexpired US passport. A first-time applicant still needs separate proof of a full Social Security number and two documents proving Indiana residency. If you thought a separate status document was needed, review this rule. Keep this in mind as you practice.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-F01","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Identity recap","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-F05","sec10-R04","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R07","sec10-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Four kinds of proof.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-F05","sec10-R04","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R07","sec10-R08"]},{"text":"Certified and unexpired.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-F05","sec10-R04","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R07","sec10-R08"]},{"text":"Show proof of any change.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-F05","sec10-R04","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R07","sec10-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us wrap up. First-time applicants bring originals or certified copies proving identity, lawful status and Social Security number, plus two residency documents, and renewing holders bring documents for a Real ID upgrade. Birth certificates must be certified government copies, not hospital souvenirs. Passports and DHS cards must be unexpired, and foreign passports need a US visa and an approved I-ninety-four. A delayed birth certificate proves identity only. Show legal proof of any name or birth date change. For citizens, identity proves status, and a Notice of Action or verified asylum proof can serve for In this lesson you will learn which documents prove your Social Security number and what to do if you do not qualify for one, the post office box rule, which documents prove Indiana residency and how recent each must be, and the Indiana Residency Affidavit for applicants who cannot provide two residency documents, including who signs it in each case. The date windows are where questions get tricky, so the lesson repeats them. Keep this in mind as you practice.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-F12","sec10-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Social Security proof","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Card, W-two, ten-ninety-nine, pay stub.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10"]},{"text":"No number: show you do not qualify.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10"]},{"text":"An I-ninety-four may be asked for.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"A Social Security number can be proven with a document showing your name and full number, such as a Social Security card, a W-two, a ten-ninety-nine or a pre-printed pay stub. An applicant not authorized to work in the US who does not qualify for a Social Security number must submit documents showing that, and may be asked for a valid I-ninety-four instead. So most applicants bring one document showing their full number, and an applicant who does not qualify brings documents showing that instead. Keep this in mind as you practice.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Addresses and date windows","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"No post office boxes, with one exception.","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"Bills, statements, pay stubs: sixty days.","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"Insurance: one year; tax forms: this year or last.","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Only applicants in the Indiana Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program may list a post office box as their residential address. A utility, credit card, doctor or hospital bill, a bank statement or a pre-printed pay stub can prove residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within sixty days of applying. A homeowner's, renter's or vehicle insurance policy proves residency if dated within one year. A W-two, property or excise tax bill, or benefits statement must be dated in the current or prior year.","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Other residency documents","fact_ids":["sec10-F14","sec10-R09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Voter card and school records.","fact_ids":["sec10-F14","sec10-R09"]},{"text":"Postal change of address confirmation.","fact_ids":["sec10-F14","sec10-R09"]}],"narration":{"text":"An Indiana voter registration card and public or private school records showing an enrolled student's name and residential address are among the accepted residency documents. A US Postal Service change of address confirmation showing both prior and current address can also prove residency. So besides bills, statements and policies, the list includes voter registration, school records and a postal change of address confirmation. Each still needs to show the right name and residential address to count toward the two residency documents.","fact_ids":["sec10-F14","sec10-R09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":32,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The residency affidavit","fact_ids":["sec10-F15","sec10-F16","sec10-R03","sec10-R10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Incapacitated, homeless, living with someone, in a vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec10-F15","sec10-F16","sec10-R03","sec10-R10"]},{"text":"Who signs depends on the case.","fact_ids":["sec10-F15","sec10-F16","sec10-R03","sec10-R10"]},{"text":"Living in a vehicle: taxes and title.","fact_ids":["sec10-F15","sec10-F16","sec10-R03","sec10-R10"]}],"narration":{"text":"An applicant without two residency documents may file an Indiana Residency Affidavit if they are incapacitated, homeless, living with a relative or friend, or living in a motor vehicle. For an applicant living with a relative or friend, that person, aged at least eighteen, signs at a branch and shows their own Indiana credential, identity proof and two Indiana address documents. For an incapacitated applicant a resident guardian or caregiver aged at least eighteen signs, while for a homeless applicant an agency or nonprofit representative signs. An applicant living in a motor vehicle needs another Indiana resident to sign and must show Indiana income tax payment and current title and registration.","fact_ids":["sec10-F15","sec10-F16","sec10-R03","sec10-R10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The date window trap","fact_ids":["sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02","sec10-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: one window for every document.","fact_ids":["sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02","sec10-F11"]},{"text":"Sixty days, one year, or this year and last.","fact_ids":["sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02","sec10-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Each kind of residency document has its own date window, and they are easy to mix up. Bills, bank statements and pay stubs must be dated within sixty days of applying. A homeowner's, renter's or vehicle insurance policy may be dated within one year. A W-two, property or excise tax bill, or benefits statement must be dated in the current or prior year. A second trap is the post office box, which is not a residential address except for applicants in the Address Confidentiality Program. Keep this in mind as you practice.","fact_ids":["sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02","sec10-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check an affidavit","fact_ids":["sec10-F15","sec10-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Living with a friend.","fact_ids":["sec10-F15","sec10-F16"]},{"text":"No residency documents.","fact_ids":["sec10-F15","sec10-F16"]},{"text":"What can you file?","fact_ids":["sec10-F15","sec10-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: you live with a friend and have no residency documents of your own. What can you file, and who signs it? Recall the affidavit rules. An applicant without two residency documents may file an Indiana Residency Affidavit if living with a relative or friend. That person, aged at least eighteen, signs at a branch and shows their own Indiana credential, identity proof and two Indiana address documents. So the answer is a Residency Affidavit signed by your friend at a branch. If you said a letter from the friend is enough, review this rule.","fact_ids":["sec10-F15","sec10-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Residency recap","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02","sec10-F14","sec10-R09","sec10-F15","sec10-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Prove your number or that you lack one.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02","sec10-F14","sec10-R09","sec10-F15","sec10-R03"]},{"text":"No post office boxes.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02","sec10-F14","sec10-R09","sec10-F15","sec10-R03"]},{"text":"Know each date window.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-F12","sec10-F13","sec10-R02","sec10-F14","sec10-R09","sec10-F15","sec10-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us wrap up. Prove your Social Security number with a card, W-two, ten-ninety-nine or pay stub, or show that you do not qualify and provide an I-ninety-four if asked. A post office box is not a residential address except in the Address Confidentiality Program. Bills, statements and pay stubs must be within sixty days, insurance policies within one year, and tax forms from the current or prior year. credentials.","fact_ids":["sec10-F17","sec10-F18","sec10-F19","sec10-F20"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on document rules and credential types.
